thesis: Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026 results, reported 2026-07-29, are a confirmed company-disclosed catalyst: adjusted EPS of $4.74 against $4.24 expected and revenue of $90.01B against $87.62B expected, with Azure growth reaccelerating to 43% and crossing $100B in annual revenue, and commercial remaining performance obligation up 84% to $678B. Shares rose about 17% the following session, and this run's own history shows a 38.1% 60-day move. The strongest counter-case for a holder is that the AI capital-expenditure build is outrunning the revenue it produces -- the concern that had left the stock down roughly 19% year-to-date going into the print. Even with capex plans unchanged and set to rise again in the new fiscal year, that read is answered by the $678B of contracted commercial RPO: the spending is against demand already signed rather than speculative capacity. No figure here is inferred from the price move.
invalidation: Azure growth decelerates back below the high-30s, or commercial RPO stops growing faster than capital expenditure, in the next quarterly report.

thesis: Corcept's Q2 2026 report on 2026-07-29 is a confirmed company-disclosed catalyst: revenue of $256.1M, up 31.7% year over year against roughly $220.1M expected, EPS of $0.36 against $0.05 expected, and $47.6M from Lifyorli in its first full quarter since FDA approval in March for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, with full-year revenue guidance raised to $1.1-1.2B. Shares rose about 22% after hours and a further 27% the next session, which accounts for this run's 45.4% 60-day move and today's print at the 52-week high. The counter-case is substantial: the December 2025 Complete Response Letter rejecting relacorilant in hypercortisolism, multiple securities class actions alleging the company misrepresented its FDA communications, and a reported federal investigation. It is answered commercially -- the raised guidance was issued after the CRL and rests on the approved oncology and existing franchises rather than the rejected indication -- but this run could not confirm whether any hearing or ruling date falls in the next ~90 days, so the legal exposure is named rather than settled and no active_litigation flag is asserted on data I do not have.
invalidation: Lifyorli's quarterly uptake stalls or full-year guidance is walked back, or a dated securities-litigation schedule emerges.

thesis: Dell produced no Step 2 signal this run (60-day move 5.8%, volume 0.69x, 15.7% below its 52-week high); this thesis exists because the position is held. The most recent confirmed company-disclosed catalyst is the quarter reported 2026-05-29: revenue up nearly 88% year over year, AI server revenue of $16.1B up 757%, adjusted EPS of $4.86 beating expectations by roughly 64%, and fiscal 2027 revenue guidance raised to $165-169B with about $60B expected from AI servers; subsequent coverage cites $12.3B of AI server orders and a record $18.4B backlog. The counter-case is memory cost inflation and the difficulty of converting that backlog while DRAM and NAND supply is tight, which the same sources flag directly and which this run cannot resolve. The next quarterly print is due within weeks -- reported as 2026-09-03, though one source implies late August -- so the catalyst that would settle the read is still pending.
invalidation: the next quarterly report shows AI server margin compressing or the backlog converting more slowly than guided.

thesis: Astera Labs' Q2 2026 report on 2026-08-04 is a confirmed company-disclosed catalyst: record revenue of $392.4M, up 104% year over year and 27% sequentially against roughly $361M expected, with Q3 guidance raised to $540-560M revenue and $1.16-1.21 EPS against a $0.73 consensus, up from a prior $355-365M revenue range. Despite that, this run measures a 30.3% 60-day decline with the stock 44.7% below its 52-week high, so a second search was run to reconcile the gap. The sources attribute it to position unwind rather than disclosed deterioration: the shares rose four sessions into the print, including 20.0% on 2026-07-30 and 12.7% the day before the report, then fell 12% on the print itself. The substantive negative in the release is non-GAAP gross margin guided down to about 72% from 74%, toward a stated 70% long-term target, alongside higher operating expense from roadmap investment. Because the drawdown reads as sentiment-driven rather than a disclosed fundamental deterioration, the evidence supports continuing to hold but does not reach a clean net read.
invalidation: gross margin guidance falls below the stated 70% long-term target, or sequential revenue growth breaks down in the next quarterly report.

thesis: Coherent's fiscal Q4 2026 results, reported 2026-08-12, are a confirmed company-disclosed catalyst, and the GAAP and non-GAAP figures are quoted together because they differ: revenue of $2.05B up 33.8% year over year, GAAP gross margin 38.5% against non-GAAP 40.2%, and GAAP diluted EPS of $1.19 against non-GAAP EPS of $1.74. Data center and communications was 79% of revenue and grew 59% year over year on the 800G and 1.6T ramp, management describes optical transceiver capacity as filled through at least 2028 with some agreements running to 2030, and fiscal 2027 guidance is 39.5-41.5% gross margin with a first $3B-plus revenue quarter expected by year end. Against that, this run measures a 32.4% 60-day decline with the stock 37.4% below its 52-week high. Nothing Coherent disclosed explains it: the drop tracks a sector-wide unwind in AI optics in which Fabrinet closed down 20% and Coherent and Applied Optoelectronics both fell double digits on 2026-08-18. That makes the drawdown sentiment-driven rather than a disclosed fundamental deterioration, which is precisely why the read does not settle.
invalidation: fiscal 2027 gross margin guidance is cut, or the disclosed transceiver backlog and capacity commitments are revised down.
sources: BigGo Finance (COHR Q4 FY2026 earnings call): https://finance.biggo.com/quote/COHR/earnings-call/US_COHR_2026-08-12

thesis: Nebius' Q2 2026 report on 2026-08-12 is a confirmed company-disclosed catalyst: revenue of $582.3M, up 454% year over year, EPS of -$0.12 against -$0.82 expected, 2026 revenue guidance of $3.0-3.4B reaffirmed, and the year-end contracted power target raised to 5GW. Separately the company announced a $27B five-year compute agreement with Meta Platforms, based on its first large-scale deployment of Nvidia Vera Rubin chips. Shares rose roughly 34% on 2026-08-12 and have since given the move back, leaving this run's 60-day figure at -17.8%. The counter-case is that the same expansion is funded with equity-linked paper: Nebius raised $5B in convertible notes to fund the build, and because that dilution is disclosed rather than speculative it is flagged rather than dismissed.
invalidation: the Meta agreement's revenue recognition slips, or further convertible or equity issuance is announced before the contracted capacity is generating revenue.

thesis: Intel's disclosed structural event this month is a $20B equity offering: 210.5M shares sold at $95 on 2026-08-12, raising the share count by about 4%, with the stock at $87.01 today -- below the offer price, leaving those buyers roughly $1.5B underwater. Foundry revenue grew 31% to about $5.8B, but external foundry revenue was only about $293M, around 5% of the segment, against an operating loss of about $2.1B. This run measures a 34.3% 60-day decline with the stock 38.9% below its 52-week high. The plausible positive is real -- improving 18A yields, which KeyBanc describes as significant progress, plus continued strategic investment -- but $293M of external foundry revenue against a $2.1B segment loss means the yield story has not yet produced customer revenue that would change the read. Several factors are contributing at once (the dilution, a reported three-decade low in CPU share, and today's broad semiconductor selloff) without one resolved as dominant, and these figures come from secondary outlets rather than a filing this run read directly.
invalidation: a named external foundry customer commits volume on 18A, or the foundry operating loss narrows materially.

thesis: Corning shows this run's largest clean drawdown among screened names: a 36.2% 60-day decline, 46.4% below its 52-week high. Two things are cited for it. The company beat revenue and earnings estimates for Q2 2026 but guided third quarter slightly below elevated consensus; and shares fell after reports that Apple scrapped its planned all-glass 20th-anniversary iPhone, a claim originating in a Jefferies note citing poor production yields rather than in any Corning or Apple disclosure. Offsetting both, Corning has secured multi-billion-dollar AI fiber supply agreements with Meta and Zayo. The decisive negative is therefore a third-party supply-chain report this run could not confirm against a company statement, layered on a broader optics-sector drawdown, and the evidence does not resolve into a clear net read. This is not a setup to enter on.
invalidation: Apple or Corning confirms or denies the all-glass programme change, or Q3 results land against the guided range.

thesis: SanDisk is down 36.1% over this run's 60-day window, after falling 56.5% from a 2026-06-25 close of $2,335.00 to $1,015.89 on 2026-07-29 -- the S&P 500's worst performer for that month -- then rebounding 26.0% the next session. The company beat fiscal Q4 2026 revenue and EPS estimates, with revenue of $8.97B, non-GAAP EPS of $39.25 and datacenter revenue of $2,977M, and has expanded multi-year New Business Model contracts carrying price floors and ceilings intended to protect margin if market prices fall. Against that, analysts caution the NAND price surge may slow, and memory names sold off broadly on 2026-08-18 as rising Treasury yields pressured the most extended trade in semiconductors. A confirmed beat and an unresolved pricing-cycle question point opposite ways, and this run cannot settle which dominates.
invalidation: contract NAND pricing rolls over in the next quarterly report, or the NBM contract floors are shown to hold realised margin through a price decline.

thesis: Micron is down 25.0% over this run's 60-day window and fell 7.1% to $897.77 on 2026-08-24 as memory names led a chip selloff. The confirmed positive is that Micron's 2026 high-bandwidth memory output is already sold at agreed price and volume. Against it sit three unresolved negatives: Netlist has brought new ITC and federal court patent actions over DDR5 RDIMMs and MRDIMMs seeking exclusion orders that could block some memory products from US import and sale; reports that US policymakers may allow domestic manufacturers to source Chinese NAND and DRAM; and a rate-driven de-rating of the whole memory complex. The evidence is genuinely offsetting, and this run could not establish a scheduled hearing or ruling date for the ITC matter, so the litigation timing is named rather than quantified.
invalidation: the ITC action produces a scheduled hearing or an exclusion order, or 2027 HBM supply is contracted on terms comparable to 2026.

thesis: Applied Optoelectronics reported a confirmed beat on 2026-08-06: a fifth straight record quarter, revenue up 86% year over year to $191.9M, adjusted EPS of $0.06 against consensus quoted at $0.01-0.02, and Q3 guidance of $255-290M revenue with $0.11-0.26 adjusted EPS. The stock nonetheless fell 15.2% on 2026-08-18, from $154.89 to $131.41, when the company filed an equity distribution agreement to sell up to $600M of common stock at prevailing market prices -- its third major ATM programme of 2026, after April and May raises that produced roughly $1.05B of gross proceeds and close to 7.8M shares. This run measures a 22.3% 60-day decline. Record growth funded by repeated equity issuance is exactly the offsetting pair the sources describe as the central debate on the name, and it does not resolve into a clear net read.
invalidation: the $600M ATM is drawn down materially, or the 800G and 1.6T capacity build is funded without further equity issuance.

thesis: Marvell reports fiscal Q2 2027 results after the close on 2026-08-27, three sessions from now, so the catalyst that would settle this read is still pending. The confirmed company-disclosed item is an expanded chip and AI agreement with Google, on which shares jumped more than 12% premarket and alongside which Marvell issued warrants to Google; JPMorgan reiterates Overweight, citing optical, switching and custom silicon demand, and the custom silicon business is expected to benefit from an early ramp of Amazon's AWS Trainium 3 programme. Against that, one analysis argues the year's strength came from interconnect rather than custom silicon -- the part of the story those programmes are meant to prove out. This run measures an 18.5% 60-day decline with the stock 30.4% below its 52-week high. Entering ahead of a print that could reverse either read is not supported.
invalidation: the 2026-08-27 report shows custom silicon revenue ramping as guided, or the Google warrants prove materially dilutive.

thesis: Rocket Lab reported record Q2 2026 results after the close on 2026-08-11: revenue of $234M, up 62% year over year, with backlog reported at $2.36B. Shares fell more than 9% premarket the next session because the company stopped short of reaffirming a first Neutron flight before year end; CEO Peter Beck said on the call that 'while the window for an end-year launch is narrowing, the work we're doing now is about risk trading, balancing the timing of our first launch against how quickly and seamlessly we can scale at tenth launch,' leaving a 2027 debut possible. This run measures a 15.4% 60-day decline with the stock 54.7% below its 52-week high. Record revenue and backlog against a slipping first flight of the vehicle the valuation rests on is an unresolved pair, and one source notes the stock still trades at 59 times revenue with Neutron unflown.
invalidation: Neutron is given a firm launch date inside 2026, or the first flight is formally moved to 2027.

thesis: AMD's confirmed company-disclosed items are strong: data center revenue up 107% in the last reported quarter, the MI400 series and Helios rack-scale systems launched at its 2026-07-23 Advancing AI event, and the first gigawatt of MI450 chips for OpenAI scheduled to ship in the second half of 2026. The stock nonetheless fell 6.6% to $482.53 on 2026-08-05 because the revenue forecast did not show AI spending converting into faster growth, erasing close to $59B of market value, and fell a further 3.3% to $457.46 on 2026-08-24 alongside a 2.83% drop in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index; SpaceX's decision to build its computing infrastructure exclusively on Nvidia chips is cited as an additional drag. This run measures a 14.2% 60-day decline. A guidance disappointment, a lost design win and a sector-wide selloff are contributing at once, with none resolved as dominant.
invalidation: the MI450 OpenAI shipments begin on schedule and lift data center guidance, or the next revenue forecast again fails to accelerate.

thesis: SpaceX is down 11.8% over this run's 60-day window. The disclosed facts point in different directions. Q2 2026 showed a narrower loss and stronger revenue, but capital expenditure rose to $18.37B from $2.83B a year earlier and the shares fell 13% on the print. Separately the stock fell 6.4% to $130.66 after Elon Musk said the company would 'probably catch the ship with the tower in a few months,' moving that Starship milestone out of the coming test flight, and the stock traded below its IPO price following a share unlock and a downgrade. One analyst calls the delay 'not that consequential' given a reusability lead described as likely a full decade ahead of peers. Heavy spending, a slipped engineering milestone and supply overhang from the unlock are contributing at once, layered on an August growth selloff in which the stock slid 4.3% with other mega-caps, and none of it resolves into a clear read.
invalidation: the next Starship test achieves the tower catch, or capital expenditure guidance is moderated.

thesis: Cerebras reported Q2 2026 on 2026-08-12 and its two revenue metrics conflict, so both are quoted: core revenue of $210M, against total revenue of $180M versus roughly $194M expected -- a miss on the headline figure. The company raised its full-year core revenue outlook to $880-890M from a prior $855-865M, and recorded a net loss of $450.5M, of which $386.6M was stock compensation. Shares fell about 14% in extended trading on the print. Since then Cerebras announced a partnership with Callosum on 2026-08-20 and general availability of CS-4 in the September quarter, and the stock has recovered enough that this run measures a +10.0% 60-day move while sitting 15.6% above its 52-week low. A raised core outlook against a headline revenue miss, with a loss dominated by stock compensation, is mixed evidence this run cannot net out.
invalidation: the September-quarter report reconciles core and total revenue, or the gap between the two widens again.

thesis: LYTE is the Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF, whose listing was approved by Cboe BZX and which launched on 2026-08-06. It qualified this run only on the 52-week-low criterion, and that reading is an artifact of its age: with 13 daily bars since inception, the '52-week' range of $24.13 to $28.91 is really an 18-day range, and today's price sits at the bottom of it. There is no company-disclosed catalyst to assess -- this is a diversified fund whose drawdown tracks the same sector-wide AI-optics unwind visible in Coherent and Applied Optoelectronics this month rather than anything specific to the instrument. The catalyst is sector-wide by construction, and the signal that surfaced it should be read as a listing artifact rather than a dislocation.
invalidation: LYTE accumulates enough history for its 52-week extremes to be meaningful, or the photonics complex stabilises.
